In summary, our research is concerned with
the design and implementation of an intelligent agent that will be able to learn and, hence, realize the optimal scheduling policy for a vehicular network that operates under an energy-limited RSU.

the design of a novel scheduling algorithm that will guarantee the continuous operation of a vehicular network, where roadside units (i.e., the RSUs) are deprived of a permanent power source and are, therefore, equipped with a large rechargeable battery.
the problem of optimizing the RSUs' scheduling policy in a vehicular network that operates in the absence of a permanent power source, and where the RSUs' batteries are recharged periodically.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed reinforcement learning approach, i.e., PEARL, is capable of providing an optimal scheduling solution for an RSU with a limited battery power source.

PEARL is a viable and effective solution to the problem of optimizing downlink traffic scheduling for an energy-limited vehicular network, where the objective is to maximize the number of served vehicles during a discharge period.

PEARL is capable of learning and, hence, exploiting the optimal scheduling policy, which is capable of maximizing the RSU's energy utilization efficiency and, thus, the RSU's operation during a discharge cycle.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the PEARL agent can be deployed in a vehicular network to optimize the downlink traffic scheduling of an energy-limited RSU, thereby maximizing network performance and ensuring the operation of the network during a discharge cycle.
PEARL is capable of achieving the best performance in terms of both RSU's throughput and vehicles' quality of experience.
PEARL is capable of learning and exploiting an optimal scheduling policy for the RSU during a discharge period that will maximize the RSU's performance while maintaining the network's operation.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the deployment of PEARL in an energy-deprived vehicular network will not only guarantee the operation of such network during a battery discharge period but will also result in the highest possible number of service requests being fulfilled by the RSU.
the proposed reinforcement learning technique can be used to train an RSU to optimize its traffic scheduling policy during a discharge cycle in an energy-limited vehicular network.
the deployment of PEARL can be a viable option to optimize the RSU's scheduling policy, especially for a vehicular network that lacks a permanent power supply.
